text:
The total amount Jim must “recover” consists of  

* the loans he takes out: \(50{,}000 \times 4 = 200{,}000\) dollars, and  
* the wages he forgoes while studying: \(25{,}000 \times 4 = 100{,}000\) dollars.  

So the financial deficit to be made up is  

\[
200{,}000 + 100{,}000 = 300{,}000\text{ dollars}.
\]

After graduating his salary is three times his former salary:

\[
\text{new salary}=3 \times 25{,}000 = 75{,}000\text{ dollars per year}.
\]

However, Jim would have continued to earn his old salary of \(25{,}000\) per year even if he had not gone to college.  The amount that actually helps him repay the deficit is the **incremental** (net) increase in earnings:

\[
\text{net annual increase}=75{,}000 - 25{,}000 = 50{,}000\text{ dollars per year}.
\]

The time required for this net increase to total the $300,000 deficit is

\[
\text{time}= \frac{300{,}000}{50{,}000}=6\text{ years}.
\]

Thus, it will take Jim **6 years** after graduation to earn an amount equal to the loans he borrowed plus the wages he missed while in school.

**Final answer:** 6
